nodes.label: A 27-year-old woman presented with elevated hepatobiliary enzymes
The patient occasionally drank alcohol and was taking axitinib, azelnidipine, and tramadol hydrochloride
The patient had no history of viral hepatitis, steatohepatitis, autoimmune liver disease, or metabolic liver disease
After stopping alcohol and axitinib, the patient's hepatobiliary enzyme levels remained unchanged
Physical examination showed no specific findings
Laboratory tests show markedly elevated ALP of 1028 U/L
Laboratory tests show markedly elevated GGT of 257 U/L
Ultrasound shows an irregular isoechoic region at the hepatic hilum
Liver biopsy shows PAX8-positive malignant cells in Glisson's capsule with bile duct destruction
Metastatic carcinoma involving the hepatic hilum is causing the cholestatic liver injury
Transaminases are only mildly elevated compared with markedly elevated ALP and GGT
MRI shows hypointensity in the hepatic hilum region
